summary: Returns the value as a non-empty two-dimensional array, or throws.
description:
The check to put in front of `Range#setValues`, which rejects a flat array with a message that names neither the
argument nor the reason. `require2DArray` throws first, with a message you control, and returns the value so the
call composes into an expression.

It accepts exactly what [`is2DArray`](is2DArray.md) accepts: a non-empty array whose every element is an array. Rows
of differing length pass — use [`requireConsistent2DArray`](requireConsistent2DArray.md) when they must match.

params.message: The exception message. Defaults to `"Expected a non-empty two-dimensional array."`

returns: the same value, typed as a two-dimensional array.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: The value is not a non-empty array of arrays.

examples.title: Validating and using in one expression
examples.body:
<tabs group="code">
<tab title="TypeScript" group-key="ts">
<code-block lang="typescript" src="require2DArray.ts" include-symbol="writeRows"/>
</tab>
<tab title="JavaScript" group-key="js">
<code-block lang="javascript">
function writeRows(sheet, values) {
  const rows = require2DArray(values, "values must be a matrix of rows");
  sheet.getRange(1, 1, rows.length, rows[0].length).setValues(rows);
}
</code-block>
</tab>
</tabs>

examples.title: What passes and what throws
examples.body:
```javascript
require2DArray([
  [1, 2],
  [3, 4]
]); // => [[1, 2], [3, 4]]
require2DArray([1, 2]); // throws IllegalArgumentException
require2DArray([]); // throws IllegalArgumentException — no rows
```
